incorporated_articles.title: Measuring the impact of AI solutions

units.text: AI outputs are not always accurate, you must verify them and manage potential harm.
units.text_start: AI outputs are not always accurate, you must verify them

units.section: Have meaningful human control at the right stages
units.text: Humans must have meaningful control over the AI system throughout the product’s lifecycle. Continuously monitor its behaviour and have plans to prevent harm. Humans must validate all high-risk decisions influenced by AI, and users must be able to report issues for human review.
units.text_start: Humans must have meaningful control over the AI system

units.section: Use the right tool for the job
units.text: Choose the most appropriate technology for your needs. Be open to AI solutions, but always consider if the problem could be solved more easily with traditional or simpler technologies.
units.text_start: always consider if the problem could be solved more easily

units.text: AI cannot replace your professional judgement or responsibility. Use it to support your work, not make decisions.
units.text_start: AI cannot replace your professional judgement or responsibility

units.text: AI is good at: summarising long documents; finding common themes across multiple documents; suggesting improvements to drafts you've written; restructuring or reformatting existing content; generating initial ideas or options to consider.
units.text_start: summarising long documents
units.text_end: generating initial ideas or options to consider

units.section: How AI should support your work
units.text: AI can support your work in two ways: support and enhance your work while you stay in control (augmentation); complete tasks independently while you review output (automation). Augmentation is the most common and valuable use of AI for professional work.
units.text_start: support and enhance your work while you stay in control (augmentation)
units.text_end: Augmentation is the most common and valuable use of AI for professional work

units.text: You might need to: sense check - does this align with your knowledge and experience? Does the logic make sense?; source check - verify (cross-reference) any cited sources, references, or legislation; check the numbers - verify statistics, dates, and figures against original sources or datasets; check with experts - ask colleagues or subject matter experts to review important or public-facing content.
units.text_start: sense check - does this align with your knowledge and experience

units.text: If you use AI to create or change official content, you must: review the content for correctness and quality; make sure it meets required standards before publishing or sharing. You're responsible for AI-generated content as if you created it yourself.
units.text_start: you must: review the content for correctness and quality
units.text_end: as if you created it yourself

units.text: Think about what information you can safely share with AI tool you’re using. For example, paid versions of tools (such as, Copilot Enterprise, or Gemini Pro) have data protection agreements. This means they can often handle personal and sensitive information safely. Check your department's guidance to understand what each tool can handle.
units.text_start: paid versions of tools (such as, Copilot Enterprise, or Gemini Pro) have data protection agreements
units.text_end: Check your department's guidance to understand what each tool can handle

units.section: AI content and Freedom of Information
units.text: If using AI in group meetings, ask for consent from participants before using AI to transcribe, summarise, or process the discussion.
units.text_start: ask for consent from participants before using AI to transcribe

units.section: Write simple prompts for everyday tasks
units.text: To write a good prompt: be specific about what you want - use direct language and action words like 'write', 'analyse', 'create' or 'list'; be specific about who it's for; be specific about the format; give relevant background.
units.text_start: be specific about what you want

units.section: Write detailed prompts for complex tasks
units.text: You can structure detailed prompts using frameworks to help you remember what information to include: RACE for focused tasks; GCSE when you have source documents; CRIT for strategic or creative tasks; PICSE for iterative workflows.
units.text_start: structure detailed prompts using frameworks

units.section: Break down complex tasks into steps
units.text: Some tasks are too complicated for a single prompt. Split them into separate steps, where each prompt builds on the output of the last (known as 'prompt chaining').
units.text_start: Split them into separate steps, where each prompt builds on the output of the last

units.text: You must check and follow your department’s AI policies, as there may be specific tools or approaches you should use
units.text_start: You must check and follow your department’s AI policies
units.text_end: specific tools or approaches you should use

units.text: Use systems provided by your department for government work, and do not include any content with personal or identifiable information.
units.text_start: do not include any content with personal or identifiable information

units.section: Choose the right tool for the task
units.text: If you do need AI, if your model allows it, pick the smallest one which will do what you need
units.text_start: pick the smallest one which will do what you need

units.text: When deciding whether to use AI, consider what you're gaining and what the environmental cost is. It's about weighing the public service benefits against the impacts with the full picture in mind.
units.text_start: weighing the public service benefits against the impacts
units.text_end: with the full picture in mind

units.section: How to monitor your environmental impact
units.text: You can use free online tools to calculate your environmental impact. Each tool serves different use cases: CodeCarbon or Carbontracker; Ecologits; Green Algorithms. Monitoring your AI product's environmental impact throughout its lifecycle helps you spot issues early and make adjustments.
units.text_start: CodeCarbon or Carbontracker
units.text_end: spot issues early and make adjustments

units.text: organisations should consider the following aspects: Technical optimisation; Data and metadata quality; Organisation and infrastructure context; Legal, security and ethical compliance. Data use must be lawful, secure and trustworthy.
units.text_start: Technical optimisation
units.text_end: Data use must be lawful, secure and trustworthy

units.text: Read the Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI. Identify datasets in your organisation that could support AI use cases. Use the self-assessment checklist. Follow the AI-ready data action plan.
units.text_start: Use the self-assessment checklist to evaluate whether your datasets are AI-ready
units.text_end: address technical, governance or legal barriers

units.text: Despite these unique characteristics, you must still: follow the Procurement Act 2023; consider data protection and security from the start; ensure fair competition (or document why you're using direct award); assess value for money; document your procurement decisions.
units.text_start: you must still: follow the Procurement Act 2023

units.text: Based on your needs you have a range of options: Exchange schemes; Pro-bono pilot competitions; Competitive Flexible Procedure; Framework call-off; Standard procurement.
units.text_start: Exchange schemes

units.text: Common myths: "It's just a pilot so procurement rules don't apply"; "Innovation means we can skip competitive process". Get commercial and legal advice early. AI procurement is not exempt from procurement law.
units.text_start: It's just a pilot so procurement rules don't apply
units.text_end: AI procurement is not exempt from procurement law

units.section: Measuring the impact of AI solutions
units.text: Measure the impact of your AI tool to check if it delivers value, meets user needs and justifies its cost. Consider: potential benefit (ROI); quality; efficiency; user satisfaction; usage; cost, savings and ROI.
units.text_start: check if it delivers value, meets user needs and justifies its cost

units.text: After release you must do regular evaluations to understand overall impact make sure the model is continuing to meet user needs
units.text_start: After release you must do regular evaluations
